paragraphs: Here's the Big Idea, friend. Psalm 23 is David, Israel's king, saying the LORD is his shepherd, so he lacks nothing (Psalm 23:1). A shepherd feeds, rests and guides his sheep, and David sees the LORD doing all of it. The grass, the quiet waters and even the care for his soul are all the LORD's work, not David's (Psalm 23:2-3).

Then comes the hard road. David walks "through the valley of the shadow of death," and he says he will "fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). Notice what changes the valley. It's not that the valley gets short or David gets tough. It's that the Shepherd is right there, and His rod and staff comfort David. Then the picture flips, and the LORD is the host who sets a table, anoints David's head with oil and fills his cup until it overflows, even with enemies watching (Psalm 23:5).

The song ends by looking at the whole road ahead. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). So here's the takeaway, baker: the one who leads you is the one who stays with you, in the green pastures and in the dark valley. And he's got a place waiting at the end. Me? I'm just glad the One who cares for sheep also cares for worn-out cookie stamps. HALLELUJAH!
